ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 75:25 ratio of light-grey/off-white (high intensity) to charcoal/black (low intensity) pixels, with dark pigmentation concentrated at the trailing edge and distal tips.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant light-intensity contiguous regions occupy the central-medial surfaces. Low-intensity pigmentation forms a thick, continuous boundary along the trailing edge, widening into solid dark regions at the distal tips. Minor dark focal clusters are scattered in the lower-central pixel coordinates of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, acute V-shaped depression with a vertex angle estimated at 35-45 degrees; the notch depth is approximately 15% of the vertical lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration pattern along the entire trailing boundary. Pixel-amplitude variations (peaks) are most pronounced at the distal tips, showing jagged, multi-directional protrusions.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curve trajectory originating from the median notch, transitioning into a jagged, roughly linear sweep towards the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-contrast, roughly circular pixel clusters (barnacles) are densely localized at the distal tips of both lobes. Smaller, isolated circular white-to-yellowish spots are visible on the interior ventral surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple low-intensity linear disruptions detected: three distinct vertical rake marks on the right lobe and several non-parallel diagonal scratches on the lower-left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on the distal tips causing physical deformation of the fluke contour; multiple vertical rake scars (likely tooth marks) on the ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: Patches of yellowish-brown discoloration (biofilm/diatom mapping) visible across the light-intensity central regions of both lobes.
